items.title: Every permutation in order

items.title: Range sums with prefix sums
items.what: Read n and q, each up to 2*10^5, then n integers (absolute value up to 10^9), then q queries l r with 1 <= l <= r <= n. Print the sum of elements l to r for each query, one per line. Build the prefix sums once, with std::partial_sum or a loop, in 64-bit integers. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Smallest value at least x
items.what: Read n, then n integers into a std::set. Then read q and q queries x. For each, print the smallest value in the set that is at least x, or -1 if there is none. Use the set's own lower_bound, not std::lower_bound, so each query is O(log n). Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: The most frequent word
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 2*10^5, then n lowercase words. Print the word that appears most often and its count. On a tie, print the alphabetically smallest such word. Count with a std::map<std::string, int>. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Cheapest merging with a priority queue
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 2*10^5, then n positive integers up to 10^9. Merging two numbers costs their sum and leaves the sum in their place.
